# The work order (CodyNote 0.30.0 and later)

When the owner asks for an update (Refresh account: "refresh <account>" and its call, email and people modes; "update the overview"), work the account in this order: some steps build on others, and the read comes last. The brief's `work_order` is the live copy. Every `codynote_suggest_changes` call carries the brief's `scan_id`; the last one's `close_scan` carries `coverage` (and the read), one entry per step: a count, `"nothing new"`, `"skipped: <why>"`, or `"not asked"` for email. The read is accepted only with complete coverage; nothing else is refused for order. The owner sees the coverage line on the scan's card, so say why when you skip.

1. Read the new material: codynote_get_customer (detail full) and codynote_map, then codynote_read with find for the passages that matter. No suggestions yet. Covers: Meetings › the new meetings, their notes and transcripts; Documents › the new files and links (their text); Overview › the current read, storylines, facts and needs-a-look, so nothing is suggested twice.
2. Email (only when asked): Only when the owner said "with email" or "catch up on email": the recipe in the brief's email block; one email record per email in the window; a follow_up for sent mail with no reply. Otherwise coverage "not asked". Records: email, email_sync, follow_up. Covers: Documents › Email: the references since the watermark.
3. People: New people the material names, changes to known ones, a role (persona) when the material makes it plain, each attendee of a call matched to a contact, a speaker label named when the transcript makes it plain ("Thanks, Dana" after Speaker 2). Then, for each person who spoke or wrote: an Observations line per thing noticed (dated, sourced), and the boxes those observations support (a sentiment line, an interest, a sore spot, background) as box / line records on card "person". Records: contact, attendee, speaker, box, line. Covers: Contacts › each contact: name, title, partner org, email, phones, LinkedIn, role (persona); Meetings › attendees matched to contacts; a OneNote transcript’s "Speaker N" labels named; People › each person’s profile: Sentiment to Panzura, Background, Personality, Interests and small talk, Sore spots, Observations (contacts and teammates); Overview › Key people (follows from the roles).
4. Account and environment: Only what was said: a version, a node count, a TB figure on the right Ring, a product they asked about. Account group, owner and RSM: never, unless a HubSpot or email source says so. Never the sentiment (the owner's). Records: company, ring, mc_reading, product_status. Covers: Overview › account row: primary and secondary cloud, last QBR, last roadmap; Overview › Environment: each Ring (name, notes, CloudFS version, nodes, object store, hypervisor, HA notes) and its MC readings; Overview › Products: status per product (discussed, purchased, implemented), quantity, ARR presented, notes.
5. Deals: A new close date, stage, forecast or term; a new opportunity; a line they asked to add. Never Closed Won or Lost: say it in the reply. Records: deal, license_line. Covers: Deals › each deal: name, HubSpot link, close date, term start and end, ARR, opp type, COLA, forecast, stage, notes, prepaid; Deals › license lines: product, quantity, unit, list and discount; Overview › strip: renewal ARR, $/TB and next renewal follow from the deals.
6. Storylines: For each storyline the material touches, in this order: a History line → Open questions ticked (with the source) or added → Helps / Hurts / Signals to watch lines → Now rewritten whole → its boxes (Goal, Done when, target date, owner, Next step) when a source says them and the owner has not typed them → status (watch with a date, resolved with an outcome). Then new storylines (kind, one line, Now, first History line, the boxes it has). Offer a split of old Notes into the lists once, when they hold Panzura angle or open questions. Records: history, tick, line, bullet, split. Covers: Overview › Storylines: kind, status (open, watch until, resolved with outcome), the one line; Overview › each storyline card: History, Open questions, Helps, Hurts, Signals to watch, Now, and its Goal, Done when, target date, owner and Next step; Overview › links from a storyline to its items and deal.
7. Action items: Fold first (recipe item.pick): read the open items and match each ask of the owner or promise from them to the open item on its topic, then update that item (a new Next step, a follow-up "waiting on ⟨name, role⟩ since ⟨date⟩" for someone else’s task that blocks it, a Context line for what was said); skip duplicates (Fathom’s two lists and the transcript are one pool), what was done or booked in the same source, calendar events and empty lines. A new item only for a new topic: title "Topic: what exactly, how much, for whom", Situation in three parts (The ask / Where it stands / Why it matters), Done when and Next step (all required), and a Context line; more than about five from one meeting means fold harder. Then bring the account’s other open items up to the rules (titles, Situations, folds, Next steps, follow-ups; an owner-typed title renamed only with something on record behind it). Handoffs to teammates. Offer a split of old Notes into the boxes once. Then check every open item (0.54.0): codynote_get_verify_brief(company, scope: "items") and its plan, every source every time, no "with email" needed (CodyNote → Fathom calls not in CodyNote → Outlook → Teams → everything new in HubSpot; a source that can’t be read is skipped and said); still open and unclear are recorded quietly, only a change waits for the owner; and a Summary where one is missing or stale. Records: action_item, box, line, follow_up, split. Covers: Action items › each item: text, due date, priority, status (active, waiting, done), teammate, deal and storyline links, sub-items; Action items › each item card: Next step, Done when, Situation (The ask / Where it stands / Why it matters), Context; Action items › follow-ups (waiting on whom, since when).
8. Company facts: Blank fields only (facts.owner_set lists the owner's), each with a source link and as-of date, from the material or web research. Records: fact. Covers: Overview › Company facts: revenue, employees, offices, HQ, industry, founded, website, acquisitions, other.
9. Knowledge: Bullets through codynote_suggest_changes as the brief says: add, update, mention, outdated. Notes at the bottom of the Overview are the owner's alone. Records: bullet. Covers: Overview › Tech stack, Workloads, Use cases bullets and their short details.
10. The read: Last. Reason over everything above as it will be once approved, plus deals, MC vs licensed, open and waiting items and the owner's sentiment (never set it). One read per scan, only when something material changed. Refused without complete coverage. Records: read. Covers: Overview › The read: health and why, renewal, what's changing, risks and openings, the one thing to do next.

```json
"coverage": {"read_material": "nothing new", "email": "not asked", "people": "nothing new", "account": "nothing new", "deals": "nothing new", "storylines": "nothing new", "items": "nothing new", "facts": "nothing new", "knowledge": "nothing new", "read": 1}
```
